speaker: Mike Torres
text: Good morning everyone. Let's start by discussing the authentication requirements for the client portal.

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Yes, absolutely. Users must be able to log in using their email address and a password. That's the baseline.

speaker: Jordan Kim
text: Should we consider social login options like Google or Microsoft?

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Not for the initial release. Email and password only. We can revisit social login in phase two.

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Passwords must be at least eight characters and include at least one number. Standard security practice.

speaker: Jordan Kim
text: I'd recommend we also require at least one special character for stronger security.

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Good point. Let's add that requirement. Passwords must include at least one special character.

speaker: Mike Torres
text: Moving on to the dashboard. What should users see when they first log in?

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: The dashboard should display a summary of their recent orders and any pending shipments.

speaker: Jordan Kim
text: Should we include notifications on the dashboard as well?

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Yes, users need to see important notifications prominently displayed on the dashboard.

speaker: Mike Torres
text: What about the notification types? Push notifications, email, or in-app only?

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: In-app notifications are sufficient for now. Email notifications can be added later based on user feedback.

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Sessions should expire after thirty minutes of inactivity. Security is important for the portal.

speaker: Mike Torres
text: That covers the main points for today. We'll document these requirements and follow up next week.

speaker: Sarah Chen
text: Perfect. Thanks everyone for the productive discussion.

speaker: Jordan Kim
text: Thank you. I'll start working on the technical specifications.
